item.title: A benchmark dataset for half-hourly evapotranspiration estimation in China from 2000 to 2024
item.description:
A benchmark dataset for half-hourly evapotranspiration estimation in China from 2000 to 2024
Long Qian, Xingjiao Yu, Lifeng Wu, Yaokui Cui, Zhitao Zhang, Junying Chen, Sumeng Ye, Xuqian Bai, Xiaogang Liu, Sien Li, and Rangjian Qiu
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6707–6740, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6707-2026, 2026
Understanding how water moves from land to the atmosphere is essential for studying climate and water resources. However, ground observations in China are often incomplete and short. We created the first seamless half-hourly dataset covering China from 2000 to 2024 by carefully filling data gaps and extending observations in time. The dataset closely matches measurements and provides a reliable foundation for climate, water, and environmental research.

item.title: Global and national lime process emissions and carbonation sink from 1930 to 2024
item.description:
Global and national lime process emissions and carbonation sink from 1930 to 2024
Longfei Bing, Xiaoyu Zhang, Le Niu, Zhi Cao, Jiaoyue Wang, Jiajie Li, Xue Jiang, and Fengming Xi
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 6741–6762, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-6741-2026, 2026
This study provides a clearer understanding of how lime production affects the climate by simultaneously assessing the carbon dioxide released during production and the amount subsequently reabsorbed. Based on historical data from 1930 to 2024 across major producing countries, we developed a comprehensive global dataset.

item.title: A convective-scale reanalysis for the ‘Swabian MOSES 2023’ field campaign
item.description:
A convective-scale reanalysis for the ‘Swabian MOSES 2023’ field campaign
Julia Thomas, Hendrik Reich, Thorsten Steinert, Gernot Geppert, Klaus Stephan, Anselm Erdmann, Philipp Gasch, Maxime Hervo, Jan Keller, Alberto Carrassi, Peter Knippertz, and Annika Oertel
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-352,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We present a convective-scale reanalysis of the 'Swabian MOSES 2023' campaign that assimilates 3-months of additional field campaign observations in southwest Germany. It is computed with a 1-hourly assimilation timestep on a 2.2 km grid centred over Germany in moderately complex terrain. In addition to all operationally available observations, it incorporates 6 additional observation types. Among these is an unprecedented number of vertical wind profiles retrieved from 12 Doppler wind lidars.

item.title: Improving seaweed cover estimation in high latitudes: a focus on kelp classification
item.description:
Improving seaweed cover estimation in high latitudes: a focus on kelp classification
Joseba Iribarren, Gerardo E. Soto, Pirjo Huovinen, and Iván Gómez
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-654,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We created the first decade-long, detailed map series of giant kelp forests across Chilean Patagonia’s Strait of Magellan. Using satellite images and high-resolution reference imagery, we tracked kelp cover from 2015 to 2025 and reduced errors caused by the low winter sun at high latitudes. The public dataset supports monitoring of these remote, valuable coastal forests and helps distinguish real ecological change from image-related effects.
